description: #749 negative controls: a pathlib constructor with a constant path, path_join with constant arguments, and trusted-anchor joins with static arguments (path.resolve(__dirname, "../templates"), path.join(__dirname, "uploads")) are path-library usage with no untrusted input flow — quoted literals are static data even when a directory name borrows untrusted vocabulary. Documentation prose mentioning path sanitization is not a code signal. Nothing fires; the provenance artifact is empty on both lists. Executable-vs-prose context is the lexical-class rule: comments and string contents (# sanitize_path handles configured paths, log.info(...)) and documentation-only files (.md/.rst/.txt) do not generate path_containment_or_sanitization or path_reference_identifier, while the same vocabulary in executable code does. Division operands end at the operand's own nesting level: sibling expressions in tuples/lists/dicts/call arguments after a pathlib / division cannot donate untrusted tokens.
diff:
+CONFIG = Path('/etc/myapp/config.yaml')
+layout = os.path.join(base, 'templates')
+const templates = path.resolve(__dirname, "../templates");
+const uploadsDir = path.join(__dirname, "uploads");
+Operators must sanitize any configured paths before use.
